references.text: The Book of Moses describes the original instructions regarding cities of refuge that were to protect those who had killed someone accidentally, and that there should be six such cities distributed throughout the land.
The text mentions that murderers may flee to the cities of refuge, which corresponds to the purpose described in Deuteronomy 19:3.
Joshua carries out God's command to establish cities of refuge and describes how a murderer must flee there and stand at the city gate.
Here are mentioned the specific cities appointed as cities of refuge, three on each side of the Jordan, in accordance with the division of the land mentioned in Deuteronomy 19:3.
Moses sets aside three cities east of the Jordan as cities of refuge for unintentional killers, as a practical fulfillment of the principle of preparing the way.
The earliest promise of a place of refuge for accidental killing, which forms the basis for the city-of-refuge system.
